Tired of having your glorious interstellar Elven kingdom being forced to use plain old mammalian ringworlds in Gigastructures? Even more frustrating is that the Gigastructures mod uses it's own ringworld setup basically preventing any custom ringworld models from being used without a patch like this, and for fans of Elves of Stellaris, the Elven ringworld is certainly a beautiful model that should not be missed out on when running it with Gigastructures.

Because of this, I have taken the time to work through the ringworld segments from the popular mod Elves of Stellaris to work with all ringworld sizes in Gigastructures. In addition to that I also took the effort to add some uniqueness to a many of the other megastructures from Gigas as well!

This is an unofficial update of NaK1119's outstanding [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1400722.7514]"Crisis Manager - End-Game Edition" mod to Stellaris version 2.7.*. 

The Unofficial Crisis Managers are an ongoing, [url=https://github.com/TehFishey/stellaris-crisis-managers]open-source project. There's a lot of work to be done on them, and current events have left me with less time to do it on than I'd like. If you'd like to contribute, or help with bugfixing, code maintainence, or localization/translation, please don't hesitate to PM me or leave a comment!

Given the complexity of this mod, not all of its features have been fully tested in the latest versions of the game. If you come across any bugs, please report them either in the comments below or on GitHub.

--------------------------------
Detailed Description
--------------------------------

Summary
This mod provides in-game tools for customizing the three main end-game crisis events, as well as the "End of the Cycle" pseudo-crisis. Among other things, it provides options to make these crises more powerful or weaker, to make them happen sooner or happen later, to allow multiple crises to happen in a single game (in series or simultaniously), and so on.

The menu can be accessed in-game through your choice of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=1087781345]!Mod Menu, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1840010432]Dynamic Mod Menu, or the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=1943060017]!! 00 Infinite Stellaris Framework (Thanks 小傘INFINI7E!). 

This mod has two companion mods, the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=2033764043]Mid-Game Edition and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=2036461392]Sleeper Edition. These mods are kept seperate for now for compatability reasons, but may be merged in the future. If you're looking for even more challenge, consider adding the (standalone) [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=2038763403]Total War Pack to your game as well - this makes crises expand far faster than normal, and compensates somewhat for their stupid AI (which, sadly, can't be modded).

This mod includes many default configuration templates, but allows users to customize each setting to their taste as well. The mod works in multiplayer (any player can access the configuration menus, though try not to do so at the same time!), but is not Achievement-friendly.

Features

Players can access the following options via an in-game menu:

[*]Configurations for multiple crisis, and the probability of each occuring.
[*]Options for force starting/stopping each crisis.
[*]Configurations for the crisis start date and the speed of their opening events.
[*]Settings to control the power, quantity, and speed of crisis ships and armies, as well as their aggression with each other.
[*]Configurations for the appearance of secondary crisis factions, as well as their strength.
[*]Configurations related to the End of the Cycle mini-crisis (including an option to force it to happen)
[*]Configurations for crisis side events (Prethoryn Queen, Terror of Contingency, Guardian Awakening, etc.)
[*]More things...


Several preset templates for all of the above settings are included. Additionally, user-designed template presets can be built as custom mods/addons; instructions for doing so can be found in the mod's directory.

Installation & Uninstallation
This mod should only be installed (or uninstalled) for games that have not had ANY crisis triggered yet (otherwise, there will be weirdness/errors/crashes).

Localization & Languages

[*]English localization needs some editing/re-writing, but is available (obviously).
[*]русские переводы завершены! Спасибо Аргокон Эстейл!
[*]已添加中文翻译。 -Lunar Traveller


If you would like to help with editing or UI cleanup, or translate Crisis Manager into your language, please let me know in the comments or a DM!

Compatibility Information
This mod is NOT COMPATIBLE with any other mod modifying end-game crises.
This mod PROBABLY NOT COMPATIBLE with any other mod modifying something about the Guardians of the Galaxy events (Fallen Empires).

Compatibility patches/changes are planned, but may take a little while. Leave a comment if there are any that you are especially interested in.

Allows you to rival anyone, since it's your decision who is your rival

Description
Why do I need bad relations with an empire just to declare them a rival?

And why should I care if they are pathetic or overwhelming compared to me?

Just makes no sense to me. If you feel the same, this is the mod for you.

This lifts the restriction on rivals so you can just rival anyone anywhere in the galaxy. Go out there and make some enemies!

What is changed in detail:
- You can also rival pathetic and overwhelming empires 
- You can rival regardless of the empire's opinion of you (no bad relations needed)
- You don't need to send an envoy to harm relations first to rival an empire 
- You don't need the Supremacist diplomatic stance to rival an empire 

This will work for players and the AI as well.

What is not changed: 
- Empires that don't do diplomacy still cannot rival others (e.g. machine exterminators or inward perfectionists)

Save Game Compatibility
Should be save to install and remove during running games (I had no problems so far).
The Rival restrictions are determined while playing the game so there should be no issues.

Mod Compatibility
Should be compatible with almost anything as it does not modify vanilla files, only overwrites some parts of files relating to rivals.

Values in files adjusted:
common\diplomatic_actions\00_actions.txt
common\game_rules\00_rules.txt
This mod does not overwrite these files in their entirety, but changes some values, and thus will be incompatible with mods that overwrite the same values.

Localisation:
None required

- None

This mod changes admiral and general uniforms to black and adds pips based upon leader rank. Hats are included for both men and women. They will randomly appear as a type of "hair" on leaders.

Under a military government, more changes occur. Rulers wear a black uniform with an eagle patch (rulers under imperial authority will wear royal garb). Governors wear a red uniform and scientists wear a teal uniform. All display rank pips.

Please note, this mod is not compatible with my other uniform collections and is likely to conflict with any other human clothing additions on the workshop. As leaders gain ranks, they will also gain pips. Basically vassalization is far more difficult than it should be. When I have such an incredibly powerful empire, the tiny empires shouldn't be so stubborn as to accept total destruction rather than a gracious vassalization.
I would like to be a gracious overlord, but they always force my hand. No more!
No more neighboring empires requirement, easier vassalization, and your friendly neighborhood fallen empires will bow before your might.
Subjects will now vote for resolutions you put up in the Galactic Community! Wouldn't want to vote down your overlord's resolution now would we? (Note: They can still vote against you in resolutions created by other empires)

Strongly recommend using this with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1813104049] Vassals Expanded and Reworked 

Consider using this mod with some other balancing mods of mine:
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1586287824] Howdy Neighbor 
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1586332122] War Diplomacy Rebalance 

This is the full list of additions

[*]Subjugation War Timer was doubled to 720 days, it always felt like it went away annoyingly fast.
[*]Vassalization no longer requires you to be "neighboring" empires, this was annoying mainly due to hyperlane chokepoints.
[*]Vassalization/Protectorate/Subsidiary modifier was reduced from -50 to -25, now AI should vassalize each other more easily and they will be less stubborn towards you.
[*]Tributary modifier was reduced from -50 to -20, it makes sense for tributary to be a more agreeable fate than pure vassalization.
[*]You can vassalize fallen/awakened empires, if you are somehow that powerful and in that good of standing why should you not be able?

Have you ever been bothered that your scientists don't upgrade their Custom AI Assistants (which were enabled by Self-Evolving Logic) to Sapient AI Assistants when you discover Positronic AI (the prerequisite technology for that trait)?  Well be frustrated no more! If all else fails and a scientist was too busy to upgrade their assistant, reassign them and the research logistics department will be sure to perform the upgrade during relocation.

Added an effect that will upgrade a leader's Custom AI Assistant trait, and then hooked in logic to call it when leaders spawn, level up, when Positronic AI is researched, and when a leader is assigned. Anything that doesn't altogether remove the Custom AI Assistant and Sapient AI Assistant traits.  This mod is implemented without changing any core Stellaris files.

NOTE: The 2.2.5 update shifted the pop growth values pretty much in line with those in this mod. I have been fairly happy with 2.2.5 growth rates, and with extensive testing I have not found an appreciably different result. However, I have updated the mod with some tweaked values (largely lowering influence of certain traits) due to popular demand.


This is a simple mod to change pop growth so it is more proportionally realistic. 

It is NOT intended to prevent diverse civilisations or long-term changes in demographic balance. The game already provides many options for being xenophobic (no migration treaties, species rights, etc) and/or horrifically, fanatically xenophobic (genocide, being generally monstrous, etc).

Savegame compatible, but best results with restart.

Remember to think in RP terms!
- If your main species is slowbreeding, sedentary, and nonadaptive. And you intend to have migration treaties with fastbreeding, nomadic, adaptive. And they have the same planet preference. And you want to use no migration or pop controls. Then expect in the long run (100s of years, but depends on your existing pop numbers etc) that on new colonies they will outbreed the starting species. The ratio will shift slowly, though.
- Remember! Pop growth in ANOTHER empire can flow into YOURS, even if it is very sedate in your own. Overflow from other civilisations is more an AI problem than weighting one.
- If you want to keep some species EXCLUSIVELY on some planets, then use migration controls.

PLEASE NOTE: If you notice anything anomalous or odd or apparently bugged, please report it in the thread in the discussions tab of this page, providing as much exact information as possible.

Major rebalance:
The latest update has majorly adjusted the weighting to solve the problems of runaway exponential growth of species with growth/migration traits and/or slight numerical superiority. See changelog for details and number.

Examples:
Species A is a slowbreeding, sedentary species.
Species B is a fastbreeding, nomadic species.
Species C is a species with no growth-related traits.

With equal starting numbers, and all else being equal:
At 80 habitability for A vs 40 for B, A will fairly rapidly outbreed B (some B pops will grow at the start, but then stop). 
At 40 habitability for A vs 80 for B, B will extremely rapidly outbreed A (very few A pops will grow).
At equal habitability, B will gradually outbreed A (after a few hundred years the ratio will be skewed maybe 3A:2B).
At equal habitability where both have the same homeworld, B will extremely gradually outbreed A.
At equal habitability where A has homeworld bonus weight and B does not, this is hard to test, but if numbers were equal to start then it would be close at the beginning, but A would eventually win out. If A already has numerical superiority they will maintain vast numerical superiority (although if they game ran for thousands of years who knows).

Introduced by migration treaty later on: 
C will rarely migrate to worlds where it has 40% habitability. 
At equal habitability C will never come to have a large pop-proportion on worlds with large numbers of A and B.
At equal habitability C will tend to be in the middle of numbers on new colonies.

External migration, refugees, and other sudden pop shifts will skew these demographics.
All of these numbers are also variable depending on growth techs, growth rates on different planets (and so internal migration).

Features: 86 Pre-Scripted Empires+
This is the expanded edition of Just More Empires, using several other flavor mods and the original JME roster of empires to vastly expand on the selection of stock pre-scripted empires. This mod works with others to offer a wide range of carefully designed, thematically consistent, and content-enriched factions to populate your games. When starting a new game, Stellaris will randomly choose empires from the roster to seed throughout the galaxy.

For the achievement compatible version of this mod, see [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1364760456]Just More Empires (Achievement Compatible). Use one or the other, not both.

01 June 18 Update: Planetary Diversity added as a dependency. All empires in the roster now have homeworld classes that fully utilize the options presented by PD.

Warning: Expect new dependencies to appear from time to time as I continue to develop this mod.

Additional Features: More Flavor
- Unique flag patterns and emblem art via Just More Flags
- New and exaggerated species traits via Just More Traits
- Earth and Deneb-based empires feature unique start screen messages and AI personalities
- Earth and Deneb-based empires communicate with each other using unique diplomatic phrases

Features In Develoment: Even More Flavor
- More unique start screen messages
- More unique AI personalities with custom diplomatic phrases
- More unique preset home systems for empires beyond Sol and Deneb
- Unique tradition options for specific empires

Dependencies: A Few
- Just More Flags (adds unique emblems and flag backgrounds)
- Just More Traits (adds 'missing' species traits to the gaps in the stock options)
- Just Name Lists (40+ thematically consistent custom name lists and growing)
- Diverse Rooms by Blackfyre (hundreds of amazing sci-fi concept art backgrounds)
- Planetary Diversity by Gatekeeper

Further Details
The random number generator (RNG) is an amazing part of Stellaris, making it possible to never encounter the same galaxy twice. If, like me however, you prefer fewer of the zany totally random creations like peacock hive minds and GEICO gekko fanatic purifiers in favor of somewhat more familiar sci-fi archetypes, then this may be the mod for you!

All 53 possible government types in Stellaris as of 2.0.4 are represented in the roster at least once, and I took care to equitably distribute species traits and civics to reduce a sense of same-ness. Regardless of your empire's ethics, the chance of encountering a hostile neighbor is as good as encountering a friendly one when playing in a Just More Empires galaxy. Homeworld types are also balanced so that all nine types of habitable planet have nearly equal representation.

There are also twelve different Earth-based empires in this mod, but only one will appear in any game (none will appear as an AI if you start on Earth as the player). Will you encounter the freedom-loving Earth Colonial Administration? The xeno-hating Divine Terran Crusade? Or perhaps the post-communist Revolutionary Union of Sol? 

You will also find six different Deneb-based Human empires, themed as alternative stories to the canon Commonwealth of Man's colonization of that system. These alternative Denebs work in the same way. Only one can appear in any galaxy. This makes for a great number of possible Earth/Deneb combinations for lots more variety in your human-to-human interstellar politics.

Compatibility: Variable

DLC/Story Packs: Inherently Compatible
In order to play as or in a galaxy with the Humanoid or Plantoid empires in this mod, you'll need to own the relevant species pack DLC. You'll need the Utopia expansion to play as or in a galaxy with any of the empires that have the Syncretic Evolution civic. You'll need Synthetic Dawn for the machine empires. Of the entire roster, however, about 60% require no DLC or expansions at all, so you're still getting over 40 pre-scripted empires for a totally vanilla copy of Stellaris.

AI, Gameplay, Graphics, GUI & Sound Mods: Probably Compatible
Mods that make significant changes to default portraits, traits, ethics, and civics may break Just More Empires (Expanded) at this time. Mods that only add to these defaults will probably work with it just fine.

Real Space: Mostly Compatible
When playing with Real Space, which is highly recommended because RS is awesome, only the Medium Sol Sector seems to be compatible with JME Sol/Earth-based empires. Do not choose the Real Space Large or Small Sol Sectors.

Sol System Expanded: Not Really Compatible
If you use Sol System Expanded starting Sol systems in your custom empires while running JME, you will likely see more than one Sol in your games.

Cultural Overhaul 2.2 Ethics-Civics: May Conflict 
Users report that this mod removes some of the JME empires.

Alternative Implementation

If you prefer granular control over which empires spawn, drop the contents of this pastebin https://pastebin.com/vpGK3DAs into your user_empire_designs.txt and disable the mod.

Overview
The [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2077186491]Machine Shipset mod is missing three entity definitions for it to properly apply its textures to permanently ruined ringworld sections. It already has the correct graphics meshes, however the entity associations for the game to find them are missing. This mod adds the three missing entities so that permanently ruined ringworld sections will can match the machine_01 graphical culture - which includes sections destroyed by The Interloper with Origin: Shattered Ring. In line with this mod's other prerequisite [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2628518102]Ringworld Graphical Enhancements, habitable Machine ringworld sections feature clouds and use the Gaia planet textures (instead of continental).

This mod also features enhancements to the Machine Shipset habitats. The tier 1 and 2 habitats have both been adjusted - T1 is color-matched to your empire flag, and T2 keeps its interior terrain after being upgraded. The T3 habitats, which are mini-ringworlds, display their terrain and feature clouds.

Note: as of Stellaris version 3.7 "Canis Minor" changes to shaders mean that Machine ringworlds and T3 habitats no longer have animated clouds.

Changes
This mod contains has four, very short new graphics entities. It also replaces fire entries from the Machine Shipset to adjust the graphics definitions to apply the above effects. All of these changes will only apply to empires with a graphical culture (shipset) of machine_01.

Compatibility
Should work with practically everything that also works with Machine Shipset.

Built for Stellaris version 3.7 "Canis Minor" and backwards-compatible with versions 3.6 "Orion," 3.5 "Fornax," 3.4 "Cepheus," 3.3 "Libra," 3.2 "Herbert," 3.1 "Lem," and 3.0 "Dick." Not compatible with achievements, but neither are the dependencies.

This mod gives you an opportunity to reform your empire into something like the Holy Roman Empire or the Galactic Republic where every system is relatively autonomous while they still remain your subject.

This mod is an updated version of [url=//steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1593716609]Decentralized Empires by George (most credit) and merged / extended version of [url=//steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2108467150]Kingmaker by Emperor Scorpio. Most of the effects and the way everything works is the same as in the original, so please see the original description for more info.

It might seem a really bad idea to split up your empire but it gives both you and your new subjects hefty bonuses to production and happiness.

Please keep in mind this release is more or less a beta. I'm releasing it now because I feel like it's mostly done, but I'm not going to promise you that you won't find some bugs. I appreciate all feedback on things that are bugged or can be improved.


Decentralization Features / Limits
 • New Subject Type: Member State (they have diplomatic freedom but pay heavy taxes).
 • New Events: Interactions with your Member States, many random events.
 • New Decision: Available to Decentralized Empires, you can ask your Member States for various amount of resources.

 • Expand your realm with the Forced Decentralization wargoal, which splits your enemy into new loyal Member States.
 • Gestalt Consciousness empires are excluded from any feature.
 • Special Decentralization ability (since 3.1): you can now switch direct control over your Member States (per Decision on your capital, not for a year if the election is lost).
 • Member States can now (3.2) be renamed (Crazy Renamer), if you have [url=//steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2458024521]Dynamic Mod Menu installed.
 • New Overlord ability: share tech and fleets with your Member States.

Note
 • This mod doesn't change any vanilla files (except wargoal 'Independence', but this is not important – 3.2) and should be compatible with most mods.
 • This mod is more or less WIP and I'll try to fix and expand it as much as I can.
 • You can change the solar system name if you like to have custom subject names (on creation, otherwise you can rename them afterwards, see above).
 • As every mod with subjects since 3.4, this is not backward compatible anymore (legacy versions are on Git).
